info.text:
$100 put in the S&P 500 at the start of 1928 grew to about $1.16 million by the end of 2025, with dividends reinvested, before inflation.
Why: companies grow earnings and pay dividends, the economy grows, and inflation lifts prices and profits.
That worked out to about 10% a year compounded (1928-2025), with 72 up years and 26 down years. The price closed 2012 below its 1999 close.
Our math: $1,000 at 7% a year for 30 years = $7,612. Past results are no promise.
Sources: NYU Stern (Damodaran) historical returns, Jan 2026; Motley Fool/Shiller data.
News and education, not financial advice.
